what: BP is a British integrated oil and gas company. It explores for and produces oil and gas, refines it, sells fuel through service stations, trades energy, and has been scaling back an earlier push into renewables.
customers: Refiners, fuel distributors, motorists at its service stations, airlines and industrial gas buyers.
money: refining, service stations, lubricants and aviation fuel
moat: Integrated positions from the wellhead to the pump, plus a trading operation that profits from price differences others cannot access.
risks: Net margin was near zero last year after impairments
Debt of about $70 billion is high for an oil company at this point in the cycle
Strategy has reversed twice, from oil to renewables and back
Oil and gas prices set profits and it does not control them
opportunities: Refocusing on oil and gas raises returns on new investment
Trading earns money whether prices rise or fall
watch: Net debt reduction and upstream production volumes.
